Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:10:1.hebrew: פטור ממיתה - דהא לא נתכוין, דאמרינן לקמן (בבא קמא מד ע"ב): כמיתת בעלים אם הרג, כן מיתת השור שהרג:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:10:1.english: Exempt from death - For [the ox] did not intend [to kill], as we say later (Bava Kamma 44b): "Like the death of the owner if he killed, so is the death of the ox that killed."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:10:2.hebrew: וחייב בכופר - דדרשינן "כופר", "אם כופר", להביא שלא בכוונה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:10:2.english: And [the owner is] liable to [pay] ransom - For we expound "ransom," "if a ransom," to include [a case where the ox killed] unintentionally.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:10:3.hebrew: ורב אמר פטור מזה ומזה - כדדריש רבא לעיל: "השור יסקל וגו'" — כל זמן שהשור בסקילה, בעלים משלמין כופר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:10:3.english: And Rav says: exempt from this and from that - As Rava expounded above: "The ox shall be stoned, etc." — as long as the ox is [subject] to stoning, the owners pay ransom.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:11:1.hebrew: והא תם הוא - אפילו למאן דדריש אם כופר, ה"מ למועד שלא בכוונה, והאי תם הוא בחיכוך זה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:11:1.english: And isn't it innocuous - Even according to the one who expounds [the verse] "if a ransom", that applies to [an ox that is] forewarned [to kill] without intent, whereas this [ox] is innocuous with respect to this rubbing.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:11:2.english: Forewarned with regard to falling on people in pits - Later, in [the chapter] Shor Shenagach et HaParah (Bava Kamma 48b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:12:1.hebrew: בשלמא התם - גבי שור שנפל על האדם בבור, איכא לתרוצי כדמתרצינן התם, דהאי דלא קטלינן ליה בנגיחות ראשונות, כגון דחזא ירוקא ונפל שלא בכוונה על זה, שראה עשב בתוך פי הבור ובא לאוכלה ונפל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:12:1.english: Granted there - Regarding an ox that fell upon a person in a pit, it is possible to answer as we answered there: that the reason we do not put it to death for the first gorings is [in a case] such as where it saw greenery and fell unintentionally upon this [person], in that it saw grass within the mouth of the pit and came to eat it and fell.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:12:2.hebrew: אלא הכא - הואיל ומועד לכך, מאי שלא מתכוין איכא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:12:2.english: But here - Since [it] is forewarned for this, what [claim of] "without intention" is there?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:13:1.english: Here also - For we see that it is rubbing for its pleasure, and not [intending] to cause it to fall upon him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:1:1.hebrew: שור באדם שעשה בו - שור קטן ההורג כשור גדול ההורג, דהא שור בן יומו קרוי שור, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ז) שור או כשב כי יולד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:1:1.english: An ox [killing] a person, where [the Torah] rendered - a small ox that kills [is treated] like a large ox that kills, for a one-day-old ox is called "an ox," as it is written (Leviticus 22:27): "When an ox or a sheep is born."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:1:2.english: Is it not logical - that [the ox] is liable to stoning in this case for a young child just as for an adult?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:2:1.hebrew: שכן חייב - בנזקין ארבעה דברים שהשור פטור מהן, ונזק לא חשיב, דהא שור נמי נזקא משלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:2:1.english: As he is liable - In [cases of] damages, [he is liable for] four things from which an ox is exempt, and [actual] damage is not counted, because an ox also pays damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:2:2.hebrew: ת"ל בן ובת - קטנים משמע, דלעיל מיניה כתיב והמית איש או אשה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:2:2.english: The verse states: "a son" and "a daughter" - [This] implies minors, for above it is written: "and it kills a man or a woman."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:3:1.english: And I have [this] only regarding a forewarned [ox] - For the verse is written regarding a forewarned [ox].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:4:1.english: You did not differentiate between an innocuous [ox] and a forewarned [ox] - With respect to stoning.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:5:1.english: Whose power is diminished with regard to damages - For if they caused damage, they pay.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:5:2.hebrew: יפה כחן - דחרש שוטה וקטן פגיעתן רעה — החובל בהן חייב, והן שחבלו באחרים פטורין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:5:2.english: Their power is enhanced - Because [regarding] a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, an encounter with them is bad — one who injures them is liable, whereas they who injured others are exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:6:1.english: But does one derive a lenient [matter] from a stringent [matter] - An innocuous [ox] from a forewarned [ox].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:6:2.hebrew: להחמיר - על הקל, דנימא כי היכי דחמור חייב, קל נמי חייב, דקדרשת תם ממועד במה מצינו. דקתני חייב באיש ואשה וחייב בבן ובת — במועד, דהא חיוב דבן ובת במועד הוא דכתיב, וקאמרת: מה חיוב דאיש ואשה (במועד) עשה בו תם כמועד, אף בן ובת נעשה בו תם כמועד. ואשתכח דקא ילפת תם ממועד, דאי לא אשכחת חיוב דבן ובת במועד, לא הוה ילפת ליה בתם מאיש ואשה, דהא במועד גופיה, אי לאו דרבינהו קרא, לא מצית לאתויינהו מדינא לעיל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:6:2.english: To be stringent - with regard to the lenient [case], that we should say: just as the stringent [case] is liable, the lenient [case] is also liable, for you are deriving an innocuous [ox] from a forewarned [ox] by mah matzinu ("just as we find"). For [the Mishnah] teaches, "[An ox] is liable for a man or a woman, and is liable for a son or a daughter" — [referring] to a forewarned [ox], since the liability for a son or a daughter is written [in the Torah] regarding a forewarned [ox]. And you say: just as [with respect to] the liability for a man or a woman (for a forewarned [ox]), [Scripture] treated an innocuous [ox] like a forewarned [ox], so too [with respect to] a son or a daughter, let us treat an innocuous [ox] like a forewarned [ox]. Thus it emerges that you are deriving an innocuous [ox] from a forewarned [ox], for if you had not found liability for a son or a daughter in [the case of] a forewarned [ox], you could not have derived it for an innocuous [ox] from [the case of] a man or a woman, because even regarding a forewarned [ox] itself, had the verse not included them, you could not have derived them by logical inference above.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:6:3.hebrew: אם החמיר - הכתוב בבן ובת, באיש ואשה, במועד כתב לך, שהרי חמור הוא לענין כופר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:6:3.english: If [Scripture] was stringent - [If] Scripture [was stringent] regarding a son and daughter [as] regarding a man and woman, it wrote [that] for you regarding a forewarned [ox], for behold, it is stringent with respect to ransom.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:6:4.hebrew: נחמיר - אנן מדינא בתם הקל, בתמיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:6:4.english: Shall we be stringent - [Shall] we [be stringent] by [logical] derivation regarding the innocuous [ox], the lenient [case]? [This is meant] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:7:1.hebrew: אם אמרת באיש ואשה - כלומר, וק"ו דדרשת נמי בסיפא פריכא הוא, דאם אמרת באיש ואשה כו'. ל"א: וכי דנין קל וחומר בן ובת שפטורין מן המצות מאיש ואשה? וזה שמעתי, וראשון מצאתי, וכשר הוא מן האחרון; דהיכי פשיטא ליה הך קולא והך חומרא דקמתמה "וכי דנין כו'", והא תנא אשכח חומרא בבן ובת, דיפה כחן בנזקין מאיש ואשה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:7:1.english: If you say [with regard to] a man or a woman - That is to say, the kal vachomer [a fortiori inference] that you expounded in the latter clause as well is refuted, for "if you say [with regard to] a man or a woman, etc." Another explanation: Can one derive via a kal vachomer [the law of] a boy or a girl, who are exempt from the mitzvot, from [that of] a man or a woman? And this [latter explanation] I heard [from my teachers], whereas the first [explanation] I found [written], and it is more sound than the latter; for how could this leniency and this stringency be so obvious to him that he asks rhetorically, "Can one derive, etc.", when the Tanna [himself] found a stringency in [the case of] a boy or a girl, whose legal power is greater with respect to damages than [that of] a man or a woman!

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:8:1.hebrew: ת"ל בן ובת - קטנים משמע, דלעיל מיניה כתיב והמית איש או אשה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:8:1.english: The verse states, "a son ... or a daughter" - [This] implies minors, for earlier [in the passage] it is written, "and it kills a man or a woman."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:8:2.hebrew: ת"ל או בן יגח או בת יגח - יגח יגח תרי זמני, דריבה לה נגיחה למועד ולתם, למיתה ולנזקין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44a:8:2.english: The verse states: “Whether it has gored a son or has gored a daughter” - [It says] “has gored,” “has gored” two times, for [Scripture] included goring [both] for a forewarned [ox] and for an innocuous [ox], [both] for death and for injury.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44a:11:1.hebrew: והא תם הוא - לא בעי למימר דמתני' כר"י הגלילי, כדמוקי שמואל מתני' בהפרה (לקמן בבא קמא דף מח:) גבי "היה אביו או בנו בתוכו", דמאי דוחקיה דשמואל לאוקמי מתניתין כר"י הגלילי? ומה פלוגתא הוה שייך בזה דהוו פליגי רב ושמואל מתני' כמאן? ועוד, דרישא דמתני' — דקתני מועד דמשלם כופר ותם פטור מן הכופר — לא אתיא כר"י הגלילי. והא דלא מוקי שמואל מתני' דלקמן במועד ליפול על בני אדם בבורות, כדמפרש מילתא דהכא במועד להתחכך על בני אדם בכתלים — משום דההוא לא שכיחא כי האי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44a:11:1.english: And isn’t it innocuous? - [The Gemara] does not want to say that our Mishnah follows R. Yose HaGelili, just as Shmuel establishes the Mishnah in [chapter] HaParah (later, Bava Kamma 48b) regarding [the case of] "his father or his son was inside it," for what would force Shmuel to establish our Mishnah according to R. Yose HaGelili, and what dispute would be relevant here such that Rav and Shmuel would argue over whom the Mishnah follows? Moreover, the first clause of the Mishnah — which teaches [regarding] a forewarned [ox] that it pays ransom, while an innocuous [ox] is exempt from ransom — does not accord with R. Yose HaGelili. And the reason Shmuel does not establish the Mishnah later as [referring to an ox] forewarned to fall on people in pits, just as he explains the case here as [referring to an ox] forewarned to rub against walls [causing them to fall] on people, is because that [scenario] is not as common as this [one].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44a:11:2.hebrew: והא תם הוא - המקשן סבור שמתחכך בכותל להפילו ולא מתכוין להפילו על בני אדם, דא"כ לא היה פטור ממיתה; ועל זה מקשה "והא תם הוא", שאפילו עשה כן כמה פעמים והרג בני אדם שלא בכוונה, אין מועד להרוג אדם, כדפי' לעיל, מדלא אשכחן מועד במתכוין להרוג את הבהמה והרג את האדם. ומשני: "במועד להתחכך על בני אדם", פירוש — במתחכך להנאתו, כדמפרש ואזיל, דהוי מועד מתחילתו והוי כאורחיה. וא"ת: ומי דוחקו לשמואל לומר שחייב כופר? יעמידנו במתכוין להפיל הכותל ולא נתכוין להפיל על בני אדם, ופטור גם מכופר לפי שהוא תם. וי"ל: דלרב ושמואל משמע להו לישנא דמתני', דקתני "ונפל על האדם", שלא היה מתכוין להפילו, אלא ממילא אירע שנפל ע"י שהיה מתחכך בו להנאתו; ולכך קאמר שמואל היכא דמתחכך בכותל להנאתו, כדמשמע לישנא דמתני', דפטור ממיתה וחייב כופר, ורב אמר פטור מזה ומזה, כדמשמע לישנא ד"פטור" שפטור לגמרי. והמקשן היה סבור דהא דנקט במתני' "ונפל על האדם" ולא קתני "להפילו", משום דלא מתכוין להפילו על האדם מיירי, אבל מ"מ במתכוין להפילו ושלא על האדם משמע ליה שמיירי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44a:11:2.english: And isn't it innocuous [tam] - The questioner assumed that [the ox] was rubbing against the wall to knock it down, though it did not intend to knock it down onto people — for if so, it would not be exempt from execution; and regarding this he asks: "And isn't it tam?" — for even if it did this several times and killed people unintentionally, it is not [considered] mu'ad to kill a person, as I explained above, since we do not find a mu'ad in [a case where it] intended to kill an animal and killed a person. And [the Gemara] answers: "[It refers to an ox] forewarned [mu'ad] to rub against people," meaning, when it rubs for its own pleasure, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain, so that it is mu'ad from the outset and it is like its normal behavior. And if you ask: What forces Shmuel to say that [the owner] is liable for ransom [kofer]? Let him establish [the Mishnah] in [a case where] it intended to knock down the wall and did not intend to knock [it] down onto people, and [thus] it is also exempt from ransom because it is a tam. And one can answer: To Rav and Shmuel, the wording of the Mishnah — which states "and it fell upon the person" — implies that it did not intend to knock it down, rather it happened on its own that it fell because it was rubbing against it for its own pleasure; and therefore Shmuel says that where it rubs against the wall for its own pleasure, as the wording of the Mishnah implies, it is exempt from execution and liable for ransom, whereas Rav says it is exempt from both [execution and ransom], as the wording "exempt" implies that it is completely exempt. And the questioner thought that the reason [the Mishnah] stated "and it fell upon the person" and did not state "to knock it down" is because it is speaking of [a case where] it did not intend to knock it down onto the person, but nevertheless it seemed to him that it is speaking of [a case where] it intended to knock it down, just not onto the person.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44a:6:1.hebrew: וכי דנין קל מחמור - פ"ה דהך פירכא אדין ראשון, דבדין שני דק"ו דאיש ואשה שהורע כחן בנזקין לא דנין קל מחמור, דאפילו אי לא הוה כתיב מועד כלל הוה ילפינן בהאי קל וחומר. אע"ג דבק"ו נמי קאמר "לא חלקת", האי לישנא לאו דוקא; ולכך אצטריך "לא אם אמרת" לעשות פירכא בדין שני שהוא ק"ו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44a:6:1.english: But does one derive a lenient [matter] from a stringent [matter] - Rashi explained that this refutation [is directed] at the first inference, for in the second inference — namely, the kal vachomer of "a man and a woman, whose power is diminished with regard to damages" — one is not deriving a lenient [matter] from a stringent [matter], since even if mu'ad were not written at all, we would derive [it] through this kal vachomer. Even though in the kal vachomer as well it says "you do not differentiate," that phrasing is not exact; and therefore "No, if you say" was needed to make a refutation against the second inference, which is a kal vachomer.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44a:8:1.hebrew: נגיחה לנזקין אצטריך - לרבות נזקין, משום דדרשינן בסיפיה דהאי קרא בנזקין בהמניח (לעיל בבא קמא דף לג.) "כמשפט" — שור בשור. וכן בסוף פרקין, לענין שמירה מעולה דנזקין, דריש מ"לא ישמרנו", אע"ג ד"לא ישמרנו" גבי מיתה כתיב:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44a:8:1.english: "Goring for injury" is necessary - To include injury, because we expound at the end of this verse regarding injury in [the chapter] HaMeniach (above, Bava Kamma 33a): "like the judgment" — [this refers to] an ox [injuring] an ox. And similarly at the end of our chapter, regarding superior guarding for injury, [the Gemara] expounds from "and he did not guard it," even though "and he did not guard it" is written regarding death.
